{
  "summary": "Demonstrates the complete removal of AssumeUTXO snapshot loading, background historical validation, and multi-chainstate infrastructure across Bitcoin Core. Consolidates ChainstateManager, block storage, P2P block downloads, indexers, and validation interface callbacks down to a single active chainstate. Eliminates dynamic cache resizing, multiple block-file cursors, the loadtxoutset RPC, and hardcoded snapshot parameters, while rejecting datadirs with incomplete snapshots at startup.",
  "problem": "Maintaining concurrent chainstates adds pervasive architectural complexity across validation, cache sizing, database lifecycles, pruning bounds, wallet scanning, and block downloading. Developers and maintainers face elevated cognitive load and subtle synchronization edge cases across core validation paths for a feature with limited real-world adoption.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description notes in-person developer consensus: 'Rough agreement about the ambiguity background validation introduces: we trust a snapshot enough to use it immediately, but describe that trust as temporary until the same node finishes checking history.'",
    "PR description highlights low adoption: 'I am not sure this amount of complexity in the most critical part of our codebase is still worth it, given that adoption isn\\'t where we hoped it would be (citing #35054).'",
    "PR description observes closing performance gaps: 'Ordinary IBD is also getting faster: #35295 is already merged, and the upcoming pruneassumevalid will make pruned IBD even faster.'"
  ],
  "dependencies": {
    "depends_on": [],
    "enables": [
      "#36557"
    ]
  },
  "scope_notes": "Author explicitly states this is a draft demonstration PR not intended to be merged directly, but meant as an architectural reference to evaluate and extract smaller, incremental PRs.",
  "changed_since_previous": "Updated the series across 34 commits following the merge of upstream test fixture cleanups (#36601), refining the deletion of the snapshot coin-insertion bypass and updating chainstate cache adjustments.",
  "card": "This draft demo showcases the complete removal of AssumeUTXO snapshot loading, background synchronization, and multi-chainstate architecture across Bitcoin Core. It collapses ChainstateManager, block downloading, cache rebalancing, and storage cursors back to a single active chainstate to illustrate code simplifications in core validation. The author notes that the demo is not intended for direct merge, but rather serves as a reference for smaller proposals such as dropping background sync. The change is motivated by low adoption, trust ambiguities with background validation, and standard IBD performance improvements.",
  "needs": [],
  "confidence": "high",
  "uncertainties": [],
  "risk": {
    "level": "high",
    "touches": [
      "validation",
      "p2p",
      "wallet",
      "rpc_api"
    ],
    "why": "Mistakes in refactoring chainstate initialization, block download scheduling, or coins database handling could cause consensus desynchronization, validation crashes, or node database corruption."
  }
}

result.summary: Demonstrates the complete removal of AssumeUTXO snapshot loading, background historical validation, and multi-chainstate infrastructure across Bitcoin Core. Consolidates ChainstateManager, block storage, P2P block downloads, indexers, and validation interface callbacks down to a single active chainstate. Eliminates dynamic cache resizing, multiple block-file cursors, the loadtxoutset RPC, and hardcoded snapshot parameters, while rejecting datadirs with incomplete snapshots at startup.
result.problem: Maintaining concurrent chainstates adds pervasive architectural complexity across validation, cache sizing, database lifecycles, pruning bounds, wallet scanning, and block downloading. Developers and maintainers face elevated cognitive load and subtle synchronization edge cases across core validation paths for a feature with limited real-world adoption.
evidence: PR description notes in-person developer consensus: 'Rough agreement about the ambiguity background validation introduces: we trust a snapshot enough to use it immediately, but describe that trust as temporary until the same node finishes checking history.'

PR description highlights low adoption: 'I am not sure this amount of complexity in the most critical part of our codebase is still worth it, given that adoption isn\'t where we hoped it would be (citing #35054).'
PR description observes closing performance gaps: 'Ordinary IBD is also getting faster: #35295 is already merged, and the upcoming pruneassumevalid will make pruned IBD even faster.'
result.scope_notes: Author explicitly states this is a draft demonstration PR not intended to be merged directly, but meant as an architectural reference to evaluate and extract smaller, incremental PRs.
result.changed_since_previous: Updated the series across 34 commits following the merge of upstream test fixture cleanups (#36601), refining the deletion of the snapshot coin-insertion bypass and updating chainstate cache adjustments.
result.card: This draft demo showcases the complete removal of AssumeUTXO snapshot loading, background synchronization, and multi-chainstate architecture across Bitcoin Core. It collapses ChainstateManager, block downloading, cache rebalancing, and storage cursors back to a single active chainstate to illustrate code simplifications in core validation. The author notes that the demo is not intended for direct merge, but rather serves as a reference for smaller proposals such as dropping background sync. The change is motivated by low adoption, trust ambiguities with background validation, and standard IBD performance improvements.

risk.why: Mistakes in refactoring chainstate initialization, block download scheduling, or coins database handling could cause consensus desynchronization, validation crashes, or node database corruption.
